Kutub-e-Khusro is an anthology of Persian poetry which was compiled by Khwaja Abdur Rahman Jami during the Sultanate period (1397 to 1485 AD). This anthology contains over seven thousand couplets, or one hundred and thirty four ghazals composed by over fifty poets from India and Iran. The original manuscript of this work is written on paper and has been preserved in the Royal Asiatic Society Library at Calcutta.

text:
"The Little Sister"

by A. T. Qureshi

One day as I walked along the road
My little sister ran to meet me;
I asked her why she came so close,
She said she wanted to see me!

When we got home that evening
There was a surprise awaiting me-
A baby brother had been born.
How did you feel, my darling?

For one thing he needed much attention,
But by and by he grew up quite tall;
And now I have him to care for
While mamma goes out to work.

Ilocano folk songs are usually about the everyday life experiences and feelings of Ilocanos. They have been passed down from generation to generation through oral tradition, making them an integral part of the culture and history of the province.

The lyrics of many traditional Ilocano songs focus on themes such as love, longing for home, and nature's beauty. These songs often tell stories that reflect the struggles and triumphs of people living in rural communities. Many songs also celebrate special occasions like harvest festivals or weddings.

text: I remember when I first met Philip as a boy. He would spend hours in our library reading books that had been deemed obsolete by most scholars—and they were often obscure tomes filled with old, antiquated language from an age long past. The only thing more remarkable than his passion for learning was his refusal to ever let anyone else see him suffer or be uncomfortable; even if it meant going without food so that he could focus on studying instead. Every day after school we'd walk home together while discussing some new theory or idea he discovered through those rare manuscripts he brought back from libraries around town.

author: robert_frost
text:
A young man came to me
With hope in his eyes;
But after a day or two
He said he was nigh through.

I tried my best to make
His prospects bright;
I told him he would get paid,
At last, in full height.

"Well," said he, "I am afraid
Of losing sight
Of all those golden hopes
That made me come up on this slope."

And now, alas! we find
It wasn't worth while;
For since he left again
To hunt for another job.

Hawai'i: A Poem

O Hawaii, O beautiful island
Where the trade winds blow and the surf is wild;
The land where rainbows dance upon hillsides green,
And gentle breezes brush my tresses keen.

With its sandy beaches and coral reefs galore,
A paradise beyond compare.
I am mesmerized by your beauty each day,
For you are home to me, I can say.
